item.title: Iran accuses UN of whitewashing US, Israeli actions
item.description:
Iran accuses UN of whitewashing US, Israeli actions

The Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson has slammed the United Nations' human rights mechanism on Iran, accusing it of attempting to "whitewash" US and Israeli actions. 

"Exploiting the so-called Special Rapporteurship on the Situation of Human Rights in Iran to blame Iran for the crimes committed by the US and Israel amounts to nothing less than a deliberate attempt to whitewash aggression, atrocities, and unilateral coercive measures", Esmaeil Baqaei said in a post on X. 

"Such an approach is deeply misleading and profoundly disingenous," he added. 

Regardless of the politically motivated nature of the mandate imposed on the Human Rights Council by the UK، exploiting the so-called Special Rapporteurship on the Situation of Human Rights in Iran to blame Iran for the crimes committed by the US and Israel amounts to nothing less than a deliberate attempt to whitewash aggression, atrocities, and unilateral coercive measures. Such an approach is deeply misleading and profoundly disingenous.

— Esmaeil Baqaei (@IRIMFA_SPOX) October 29, 2026

item.title: More on tanker set ablaze in Hormuz Strait
item.description:
More on tanker set ablaze in Hormuz Strait

A tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was hit by a small boat with two explosive devices attached to its hull, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said in an update on Friday.

This caused blasts and sparked a fire in the vessel's engine room that temporarily disabled it. 

According to UKMTO, the crew were safe, there was no environmental impact and the fire had been extinguished. The vessel is now continuing to its next port of call.

There was no immediate answer as to who was behind the attack. 

Earlier, we reported that the tanker, transiting outbound in the Strait of Hormuz, was on fire. The incident occurred 25 nautical miles north east of Oman's Khasab.

item.title: US Treasury chief claims Iran 'running out of' economic lifelines
item.description:
US Treasury chief claims Iran 'running out of' economic lifelines

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent claimed that Iran is "running out of" economic lifelines amid Washington's sanctions on Tehran. 

"Under Operation Economic Outcast, Iran’s regime is running out of lifelines, and its proxies are feeling the pressure," he said in a post on X. 

He further claimed that the country is "struggling to move money, while the IRGC is reportedly failing to pay its own troops".

"We are cutting the regime’s ability to fund the Houthis, Hamas, and Hizballah. We will not allow Tehran to continue financing their campaign of terror," Bessent added.

Under Operation Economic Outcast, Iran’s regime is running out of lifelines, and its proxies are feeling the pressure. Tehran is struggling to move money, while the IRGC is reportedly failing to pay its own troops. We are cutting the regime’s ability to fund the Houthis, Hamas, and Hizballah. We will not allow Tehran to continue financing their campaign of terror.

— Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent (@SecScottBessent) October 30, 2026

item.title: JD Vance letter may offer last chance to avert fresh conflict between US and Iran
item.description:
US vice-president writes to top Iranian security official in sign Washington has not abandoned diplomacy

Hopes of averting a major new conflagration between Iran and the US soon after Tuesday’s midterm elections could rest on Iran’s response to a personal letter from the US vice-president, JD Vance, offering to restart diplomacy.

The letter, written after predominantly Qatari mediation, was sent to the secretary of Iran’s supreme national security council, Mohsen Rezaei on Sunday. It requires Tehran to agree to make commitments on its nuclear programme at the start of a process that would lead to the opening of the strait of Hormuz within seven days in return for US sanctions relief.

item.title: Seven oil tankers carrying 288,000 tonnes of Russian diesel sail towards US
item.description:
Tankers, tracked by Greenpeace, are first phase of Trump-Putin deal – but there is uncertainty over whether they will unload

Seven oil tankers carrying an estimated 288,000 tonnes of Russian diesel are now sailing towards the US, though it is uncertain if the vessels will be able to unload amid a political row about the legality of the shipments.

The transport, tracked by the pressure group Greenpeace, is the first phase of a contentious supply deal negotiated between presidents Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin earlier this month, reversing years of sanctions on Russia oil.

item.title: Cuts like a knife: Canadian rocker Bryan Adams trolls Trump with new song
item.description:
Musician wrote a ‘love letter’ to Canada with a new album – and some pointed commentary about the US president

Lake Ontario, the vast body of water that straddles the US-Canada border, has gone by many names over the centuries: Lac Saint-Louis, Lacus Ontarius, Skaniadorio, Cataraqui Lake. But one thing it will never be called, says the Canadian rock star Bryan Adams, is Lake America.

In his new song Lake Ontario, Adams takes aim at the US president, Donald Trump, accusing him of “breaking the peace” between the people who live on the lake’s shores.

The ‘lake of shining waters’ is what the Iroquois called her

It’s a First Nations name – not an executive order.

But things weren’t going his way in Iran

So like a baby tossing the toys from the pram

You can push us to the brink

But where the open road divides
